recheck_why: I tried to split the cluster into a hill and a village, or a site and its museum. It does not split. The hill item Q767809 has its own point on the ridge at 52.3978, 8.1125, about 1.6 km away. Yet both records stand 7 m apart at 52.408, 8.129, in the lowland gap at the Oberesch find site beside Museum und Park Kalkriese. Both texts are about one thing: the Roman find site in the pass between the Kalkrieser Berg and the Grosses Moor, taken to be the Varus battlefield. Neither record is the modern village or the museum. On the map this is one site twice. The find region has an item of its own, Q106519739 (dewiki 'Fundregion Kalkriese'), and neither record carries it, so no record's item is the site's own. The survivor stays 'Kalkriese': the common name of the battlefield, the text that covers the excavations and finds, 16 images against 1. Fixing the item link is a job for the link repair. Note that the de article calls the identification with the Varus battle disputed (the battle of Caecina is the alternative), which concerns the text, not this merge.
why: Both records stand on one point (7 m apart, both at the Kalkriese find site, Wikidata P625 of Kalkriese 52.408056, 8.129444) and both describe one archaeological site: the Roman battlefield at Kalkriese below the Kalkrieser Berg, identified as the likely site of the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest. The Kalkriese article names the Kalkrieser Berg as that site, and Wikidata labels the hill item Q767809 in English simply 'Kalkriese'. Neither item is the find site's own (Q60176450 is the village, Q767809 the hill; de article 'Fundregion Kalkriese' covers the find region), so that link is a matter for the link repair, not for this verdict. Survivor 3911fbf9: 'Kalkriese' is the name the battlefield is commonly called in English, its Wikipedia-based text covers the excavations and finds, 16 images against 1; content links are equal (5 and 5).
